name: Jeonnam/Gwangyang Cloud Data Center at Hwanggeum Industrial Complex
developer: Jeonnam Cloud Data Center Co.; KT; Microsoft Korea; Gwangyang GI
notes: Gwangyang Bay Area Free Economic Zone notice says a 40MW hyperscale cloud data center is being built in Gwangyang Hwanggeum Industrial Complex. Yonhap reported the 2023 investment agreement and target completion by end-2025; ETNews later reported a project task force, 750 billion KRW investment, and two 20MW facilities with October 2024 groundbreaking target. No later completion confirmation found in this pass.

name: Solaseado RE100 Data Center Park / 1GW campus
developer: Jeollanam-do; Haenam County; Bosung Group / Seonamhaean Enterprise City Development; TGK / Diode Ventures
notes: Large-scale Solaseado/Guseong district plan in Haenam-gun. Reporting describes phased buildout to 25 x 40MW data centers, with early phase buildings and substations before 2037. Treat as campus-level planned capacity rather than a single building.

name: TGK / Bosung Solaseado RE100 Data Center Cluster phase
developer: Bosung Group; TGK; Diode Ventures; EIP Asset Management
notes: Initial Solaseado phase announced through a $2bn investment agreement: five 40MW RE100 data center buildings, total 200MW, at Solaseado in Haenam. Related sources describe later expansion to the wider 1GW park.

name: National AI Computing Center at Solaseado Data Center Park
developer: Samsung SDS-led consortium / KOACC; Ministry of Science and ICT; Naver Cloud
notes: Samsung SDS said the consortium selected and inspected the Haenam Solaseado site. Government and industry reports say MSIT held the groundbreaking on 2026-08-03 at Solaseado Data Center Park, with completion targeted in 2028. Local reports cite 40MW and roughly 15,000 AI semiconductors/GPUs.

name: Samsung Haenam Solaseado AI Data Center expansion plan
notes: Seoul Economic Daily reported Samsung's public plan to invest 17 trillion KRW at Haenam Solaseado for a 210MW AI data center, targeting first operation in 2028; article says this scales beyond the 40MW government-backed National AI Computing Center. Capacity in Korean source is written as MV but context indicates MW.

name: Hampyeong Wolya Global Data Center Cluster
notes: Hampyeong County and Jeollanam-do agreed to pursue a future regional development package including a data-center concentration district. 2025 report cites attracting five 40MW operators; 2023 semiconductor-special-zone reporting described a larger target of 20 x 40MW, 800MW, at Wolya General Industrial Complex. Marked planned because no named operator or permit was found.

name: Jangseong Pine Data Center
developer: Fine/Pine DCPFV; CJ OliveNetworks; Daewoo Engineering & Construction; Pine & Partners Asset Management; Hyundai Motor Securities
notes: Groundbreaking held 2025-12-15 in Nam-myeon Advanced 3 District. Initial phase is reported as 26MW, 395.9 billion KRW, with target operation in first half of 2028; some earlier agreement sources referenced a 40MW Kakao Enterprise plan, now apparently restructured as Pine Data Center.

name: Daewoo/KT/Benefos Jangseong AI Data Center
developer: Benefos; Daewoo Engineering & Construction; KT; Top Solar; Jeollanam-do; Jangseong County
notes: Jeollanam-do, Jangseong County, Gangjin County and private participants signed an MOU for a 500MW AI data center program split into 200MW in Jangseong and 300MW in Gangjin. Later Sedaily English report said permitting was underway with groundbreaking targeted for the following year.
